dedupe_keys.name: fhwa emergency relief resilience case studies resilience betterments after disasters

description: The Federal Highway Administration and state departments of transportation developed case studies on how resilience betterments were built into the repair and reconstruction of federal-aid roads damaged by natural disasters, funded by FHWA's Emergency Relief program to reduce future damage and costs. Seven case studies are listed with facility, hazards and a summary: a landslide repair on US Highway 231 in Alabama replaced by two bridges; a longer bridge with gabion training dikes at Beaver Dam Wash, Arizona; post-fire flood mitigation of detention basins and a bridge in Arizona; rockfall fences in Colorado sized by modelled debris flows; an articulating concrete block revetment on a Florida coastal highway after Hurricane Michael; replacement and rehabilitation of three historic bridges in Hawaii against flood and landslide; and tied concrete block matting against erosion of flood-prone Iowa roadways, with cost-effectiveness analyses. Coverage is national (United States). The case studies are free to read and download from the FHWA web page, last updated in September 2023. Caveats: they are short project summaries with the state's own analyses, not a systematic evaluation, and measured post-project performance is not reported. They document recovery and adaptation choices useful for parameterising restoration and adaptation options in road resilience models. They complement the Caltrans wildfire vulnerability analysis and are related to the Hawaii coastal highway program data.
